newsitem.title: USA: Hartmarx Q1 pretax earnings improve.
newsitem.headline: Hartmarx Q1 pretax earnings improve.

text.p: Hartmarx Corp said Wednesday a $4.74 million improvement in its first quarter pretax earnings was due to better gross margins on higher sales, a lower operating expense ratio and reduced interest costs.
Its pretax earnings for the first quarter ended February 28 amounted to $2,170,000, compared with a year-ago pretax loss of $2,570,000. Sales for the quarter rose to $177,118,000 from $150,859.
Net earnings in the first quarter of $0.04 a share compared with a year-ago loss of $0.05 before an extraordinary gain.

Hartmarx said the Plaid brands acquired in November 1996 contributed significantly to revenues, while earnings benefited from strong performances by Hart Schaffner & Marx and Hickey-Freeman in the menswear group, as well as by womenswear units Barrie Pace and International Women's Apparel.
Operating expense reductions taken last year generated savings in every major unit.
"We have broadened product offerings by entering new markets with our strongest brands," Elbert Hand, chairman, said in a statement.
Shareholders' equity increased by $20 million in the past 12 months, to $4.90 a share currently, while debt declined by $11 million, even after the $27 million paid for Plaid assets.

"Equity should exceed debt by year-end and the balance sheet will be in the best condition it has been in this decade," Hand said. "Acquisitions and new ventures have been funded by cash generated from our current operating companies through higher earnings and improved utilization of working capital."
